## Exercise (bonus)

Remember the [**previous exercise**](https://biodiversitydata.github.io/data-access/#/exercise). We worked with two datasets: the **herbarium** 
data the **GBIF occurrences**. In this exercise, we are going to **clean** each 
dataset and **merge** them into a single dataset.

<br><br>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}
#### **Part 4 - Check coordinates**

{{< fa circle-arrow-right >}}&nbsp; Some coordinates are outside Guatemala. Remove
these data by filtering coordinates w/ the spatial extent of Guatemala:
  
- Longitude min = `-92.22925`
- Longitude max = `-88.22502`
- Latitude min = `13.73534`
- Latitude max = `17.81933`
:::

::: {.column .fragment width=50%}
#### **Part 5 - Map occurrences**

{{< fa circle-arrow-right >}}&nbsp; Convert the data.frame in a spatial vector (package `sf`) defined under the CRS `EPSG 4326`

{{< fa circle-arrow-right >}}&nbsp; Get spatial boundaries of Guatemala (w/ `rnaturalearth::ne_countries()`)

{{< fa circle-arrow-right >}}&nbsp; Make a map w/ `ggplot2`
:::

## Correction

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=48%}
#### **Part 1 - Clean herbarium data**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Import herbarium data ----
herbarium <- read.csv2("UC1-3c-open-refine.csv")

## Clean data ----
herbarium <- herbarium |>

  janitor::clean_names() |>

  dplyr::select(country_col, full_name, lat, lon) |>

  dplyr::mutate(country_col = stringr::str_squish(country_col)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(full_name = stringr::str_squish(full_name)) |>

  dplyr::mutate(lon = parzer::parse_lon(lon)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(lat = parzer::parse_lat(lat)) |>

  dplyr::filter(
    full_name %in% c("Catopsis sessiliflora", "Catopsis nutans")
  )
```

<br>

::: {.fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Check data ----
anyNA(herbarium$country_col)
unique(herbarium$country_col)

anyNA(herbarium$full_name)
unique(herbarium$full_name)

anyNA(herbarium$lon)
range(herbarium$lon)

anyNA(herbarium$lat)
range(herbarium$lat)
```
:::
:::

::: {.column width=4%}

:::

::: {.column .fragment width=48%}
#### **Part 2 - Clean GBIF occurrences**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Import GBIF occurrences data ----
gbif_occ <- readxl::read_xlsx("gbif_occurrences.xlsx")

## Clean data ----
gbif_occ <- gbif_occ |>

  janitor::clean_names() |>

  dplyr::mutate(
    scientific_name = stringr::str_replace(
      scientific_name,
      "^([[:alpha:]]+\\s+[[:alpha:]]+).*",
      "\\1"
    )
  )
```
<br>

::: {.fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Check data ----
anyNA(gbif_occ$scientific_name)
unique(gbif_occ$scientific_name)

anyNA(gbif_occ$country)
unique(gbif_occ$country)

anyNA(gbif_occ$decimal_longitude)
range(gbif_occ$decimal_longitude)

anyNA(gbif_occ$decimal_latitude)
range(gbif_occ$decimal_latitude)
```
:::
:::

::::

## Correction

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=48%}
#### **Part 3 - Row bind the two datasets**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Rename herbarium columns ----
herbarium <- herbarium |>
  dplyr::rename(
    country = country_col,
    scientific_name = full_name,
    decimal_latitude = lat,
    decimal_longitude = lon
  )
```

<br>

::: {.fragment}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Row binds the two datasets ----
final <- dplyr::bind_rows(herbarium, gbif_occ)
```
:::

:::

:::

## Correction (bonus)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=48%}
#### **Part 4 - Check coordinates**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Filter coordinates based on Guatemala extent ----
final <- final |>

  dplyr::filter(
    decimal_longitude >= -92.22925,
    decimal_longitude <= -88.22502,
    decimal_latitude >= 13.73534,
    decimal_latitude <= 17.81933
  )
```

<br>

::: {.fragment}

#### **Part 5 - Map occurrences**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Convert data.frame into sf object ----
final_sf <- final |>
  sf::st_as_sf(
    coords = c("decimal_longitude", "decimal_latitude"),
    crs = 4326
  )

## Get Guatemala boundaries ----
gtm <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(country = "Guatemala")

## Plot map ----
ggplot2::ggplot(data = gtm) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf() +

  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    data = final_sf,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(color = scientific_name)
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```
:::
